conflicts: Energy of 6d7s7p 4F°3/2: Zhang et al. 2020 measured 13712.74(3) cm^-1, 0.16 cm^-1 below the value 13712.898(11) from Meggers' grating spectra. Kramida 2022 attributes the laser value to distorted hyperfine intensities and reports that the Mainz group later confirmed the Meggers value; the NIST energy is kept and no measured_energy_cm is given for this level.
A(6d7s7p 2P°3/2, 26066 cm^-1) of 227Ac: Table 7 of Sonnenschein's thesis gives -990.6(12) and -1002.0(108) MHz, the text gives the mean as +990.7(12) MHz. The negative sign of the table is used.

Isotope shift of the 438.58 nm line: Ferrer et al. 2017 print delta-nu(227,215) = 58,319(19)(133) MHz (positive), Verstraelen et al. 2019 quote the same result as -58.3 GHz and give negative shifts for 225-229Ac relative to 215Ac. With F = -39 GHz/fm^2 and a larger radius for heavier isotopes the Verstraelen sign corresponds to nu(A) - nu(215); the 212-214Ac entries are stored as printed by Ferrer and their sign is not verified.

Magnetic moments of 225-229Ac: collinear spectroscopy of Ac+ (Li et al. 2025) gives 1.482, 1.278, 1.320, 2.007 mu_N (10 % theory uncertainty) for 225, 226, 228, 229Ac; in-source spectroscopy scaled to 215Ac (Verstraelen et al. 2019) gave 1.330(19){40}, 1.06(4){3}, 1.10(9){30}, 1.82(3){7} mu_N and 1.220(18){30} for 227Ac, against 1.07(18) from Ferrer et al. The file keeps Ferrer for 227Ac and Li for the others.

a(4P°5/2) of 225Ac: 2290(4){6} MHz (high-resolution, quoted) vs 2269(6){21} and 2243(9){47} MHz (in-source, two runs); of 227Ac: 2104.8 (Ferrer, Sonnenschein), 2105(3){5} (quoted), 2084(31){21} and 2176(27){71} MHz (in-source).
Ionization energy: 43394.45(19) cm^-1 (Rossnagel et al. 2012) vs 43394.52(10) cm^-1 (Kramida's re-fit of the same data, adopted by NIST); consistent.

J of the 22801.11 cm^-1 level: Meggers assigned 3/2; the hyperfine structure shows J = 5/2 (Ferrer 2017, Granados 2017, Sonnenschein 2015), as NIST now lists. Kramida 2022 also rejects the Meggers levels at 23475.94 and 26533.16 cm^-1.

notes: Actinium has no stable isotope; the site isotope is presumably 227Ac (I = 3/2, 21.77 y). Hyperfine constants from Sonnenschein's thesis carry statistical errors only. In Ferrer/Granados the first bracket is a 2-sigma statistical error and the second a systematic one; where one 'unc' is given here the two were combined in quadrature. Isotope shifts are stored as nu(first) - nu(second) following Verstraelen et al.; see the conflict about the sign in Ferrer et al. Second-step lines of the resonance ionization scheme (434.51 nm, 424.69 nm from the 22801 cm^-1 level) end on autoionizing states that are not in the NIST level list and are not entered. Transition probabilities shown on the site come from NIST ASD, whose Ac I data appear to follow Kramida 2022 (mostly scaled Cowan-code calculations, normalised to the three measured lifetimes).
